items.name: Pacific Grove Monarch Sanctuary
items.best_time: November–January. Before 11 AM or on overcast days under 55°F for clusters; after 11 AM on sunny days for monarchs in flight around the lower nectar beds. Museum docents are usually on site 11 AM–3 PM, October–February.
items.description: Open, ADA-accessible grove with a packed-gravel path where western monarch butterflies overwinter from about mid-October to February; the largest overwintering site in Monterey County.
items.notes: No pets, food or smoking; stay on the paths and don't touch the butterflies (fines up to $1,000). Free but limited street parking; no bus parking. Closes only in dangerously high winds.

items.name: Pacific Grove Museum of Natural History
items.cost: Adults $15; youth 4–18, students, seniors 65+ and military/veterans $10; free for Monterey County residents (with ID), members and ages 3 and under
items.description: Small natural history museum downtown covering Central Coast wildlife, plants, geology and culture, with a native plant garden and the museum's monarch butterfly program.
items.notes: Closed Fourth of July, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day. A Monterey Bay Aquarium ticket from the past 48 hours gets $2 off. Groups of 10+ should contact the museum ahead.

items.name: Point Pinos Lighthouse
items.cost: $7 over age 17; $3 ages 7–17; under 7 free (tickets on site)
items.description: Lighthouse at the northern tip of the Monterey Peninsula, lit nightly since February 1, 1855 and billed by the city as the oldest continuously operating lighthouse on the West Coast; still an active aid to navigation.
items.notes: Closed Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving, Dec 25 and Jan 1. No dogs except service dogs, no drones without a permit, and bikes must be walked to the rack.

items.name: Lovers Point Park & Beach
items.address: Ocean View Blvd. and 17th St., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: Landscaped waterfront park at the foot of 17th Street with a lawn, sandy coves, rocky outcrops, a concrete pier, a beach volleyball court and a children's pool; used for swimming, surfing, diving and picnics.
items.notes: The Stillwell Children's Pool is closed for the season and reopens summer 2027. Waters offshore are a no-take marine reserve (Lovers Point–Julia Platt SMR). Weddings need a city reservation and permits.

items.name: Asilomar State Beach
items.best_time: Low tide for tidepools; stay well back from the surf on high-swell days.
items.description: Day-use state beach of white sand and rocky tidepool coves along Sunset Drive, backed by the Asilomar Dunes Natural Preserve and next to the Asilomar Conference Grounds.
items.notes: Leashed dogs allowed. Offshore is Asilomar State Marine Reserve: no collecting or fishing. State Parks closes the beach and Coast Trail during large swells.

items.name: Pacific Grove Marine Gardens tidepools (Point Pinos)
items.address: Ocean View Blvd., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: Protected stretch of rocky shore, tidepools and kelp forest running about 1.5 miles from Lovers Point to Point Pinos, where low tide exposes sea stars, anemones, crabs and nudibranchs.
items.notes: State Marine Conservation Area: it is illegal to take or disturb any marine life, rocks or shells; only recreational finfish fishing is allowed. Exposed to big waves.

items.name: Shoreline Park & Ocean View Boulevard
items.address: Ocean View Blvd., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: The city's continuous public waterfront from Hopkins Marine Station around the point to Asilomar State Beach, with turnouts, picnic spots and viewpoints along Ocean View Boulevard.
items.notes: Taking marine wildlife is generally prohibited along the Pacific Grove coast; finfish fishing only between Point Pinos Lighthouse and the east end of Perkins Park. Keep 100 yards from seals, sea lions and otters; feeding wildlife is illegal in the city.

items.name: Perkins Park
items.address: Ocean View Blvd. between Lovers Point and the Esplanade, Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: Shoreline strip between Lovers Point and the Esplanade with stone terrace walls, walking paths and the "magic carpet" ice plant first planted here by resident Hayes Perkins.

items.name: Berwick Park
items.address: Ocean View Blvd. and 9th St., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: One-acre bayfront lawn on Ocean View Boulevard with rocky outcrops, native plantings and wide views across Monterey Bay.
items.notes: Weddings need a city reservation and permits.

items.name: Monterey Bay Coastal Recreation Trail (Pacific Grove section)
items.address: Ocean View Blvd., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: About one mile of former railroad right-of-way from the Monterey Bay Aquarium to Lovers Point, with separate walking and bike paths; part of the trail network that runs to Marina.

items.name: Asilomar Coast Trail
items.best_time: Low tide to pair the walk with tidepools.
items.description: Coastal path above Asilomar State Beach running along sandy coves and rocky tidepools below the Asilomar Dunes preserve, with views over Asilomar State Marine Reserve.
items.notes: Leashed dogs allowed. Parking along Sunset Drive. Closed by State Parks during large swells.

items.name: Lynn "Rip" Van Winkle Open Space
items.address: Congress Avenue between Sunset Drive and Forest Lodge Road, Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: Twenty-acre ribbon of rugged Monterey pine, cypress and oak forest along Congress Avenue, used by walkers and joggers, with pedestrian access into Pebble Beach and 17-Mile Drive.
items.notes: Popular for off-leash dog walking.

items.name: Pacific Grove Golf Links
items.cost: 18 holes walking $66 Mon–Thu, $89 Fri–Sun and holidays; twilight $46/$59; juniors (17 and under) $20/$30; electric cart $25 per rider for 18 holes
items.hours: Sunrise to sunset, 7 days a week
items.description: Municipal 18-hole course opened in 1932, with a cypress-lined front nine and an oceanside back nine cut through windswept dunes.
items.notes: Book tee times by phone (831-648-5775) or online.

items.name: Crespi Pond
items.description: Small freshwater pond at Point Pinos on the edge of the golf links just past the lighthouse, named for Father Crespí, whose diaries from the 1769 Franciscan expedition mention it.

items.name: Caledonia Park
items.description: Neighborhood park behind the post office, a block from downtown, with a tot area, an ADA-accessible playground, climbing equipment, a ballfield, a basketball court, picnic tables and restrooms.

items.name: George Washington Park
items.address: Short St. to Sinex Ave. between Melrose and Alder Sts., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: The city's largest park: six blocks of mostly natural forest with wildlife habitat and trails, plus a large play structure, picnic tables, barbecue grills, restrooms and a ballfield.
items.notes: Individual picnic tables are first come, first served; the group picnic area, barbecue pit and ballfield need a permit (Recreation, 831-648-3134).

items.name: Asilomar Conference Grounds & Dunes Boardwalk
items.best_time: Fri–Sat for the State Parks ranger-led walks (Asilomar Origins 10 AM, Dunes Walk 3 PM); bird walk 9 AM on the second Sunday of each month.
items.description: Historic conference grounds in Asilomar State Beach with buildings by Julia Morgan, free self-guided architecture tours via scan stations, and a quarter-mile boardwalk loop through the restored dunes.
items.notes: Ranger tours depend on staff availability; the schedule is posted at the State Park desk in the Phoebe A. Hearst Social Hall, where advance sign-up is recommended. Leashed dogs are allowed on the grounds but not in buildings.

items.name: Jewell Park
items.address: Central Ave. and Grand Ave., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: Downtown lawn park with specimen trees and a gazebo, next to the library and the Museum of Natural History, and home of the small "Little House" meeting building.
items.notes: The gazebo and Little House need a city use permit.

items.name: Pacific Grove Museum-Gallery (Trotter Galleries)
items.hours: Tue–Sat 12–4 PM; other times by appointment or chance
items.description: Free 4,000-square-foot gallery across from City Hall showing early California art and displays on regional history and writers such as Steinbeck and Robert Louis Stevenson.
items.notes: Run by a private fine-art dealer (Trotter Galleries).

items.name: Pacific Grove Certified Farmers Market
items.address: Central Ave. and Grand Ave., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.description: Weekly Monday farmers market downtown at Central and Grand, run by Everyone's Harvest, open rain or shine.
items.notes: Open year-round except about two weeks over Christmas and New Year's (last 2026 market Dec 14; returns Jan 4, 2027). Accepts EBT, WIC and Senior FMNP, with Market Match. Service animals only.

items.name: Downtown Pacific Grove (Lighthouse Avenue)
items.description: Pacific Grove's walkable downtown of boutiques, stores and restaurants, a few blocks up from Lovers Point.
items.notes: Shops and restaurants set their own hours.

items.name: Pacific Grove Public Library
items.hours: Mon 2–6 PM; Tue–Thu 10 AM–6 PM; Fri–Sat 10 AM–5 PM; closed Sun
items.description: City library next to Jewell Park downtown, with storytimes and family programs.
items.notes: Closes for city holidays; check the library's notices before a holiday visit.

items.name: Pacific Grove Art Center
items.hours: Wed–Sat 12–5 PM; Sun 1–4 PM; closed Mon–Tue
items.description: Community art center since 1969 with four exhibit galleries that change every other month, 17 artist studios and classes for adults and kids.
items.notes: The center's contact page lists different hours (Wed–Sun 12–4 PM) than its home page.

items.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
items.cost: Adults (18–69) $65; youth (5–17) $50; seniors (70+) $50; ages 4 and under free
items.description: Large public aquarium at the Pacific Grove end of Cannery Row, reachable on foot via the Coastal Recreation Trail, with Monterey Bay habitat exhibits and scheduled feedings.
items.notes: Hours vary by day; check the aquarium's schedule. Keep your ticket for $2 off at the Pacific Grove Museum of Natural History within 48 hours.

items.name: Cannery Row
items.description: Monterey's historic sardine-cannery waterfront, now lined with hotels, restaurants and shops, starting just east of the Pacific Grove line.
items.notes: A public street: businesses set their own hours.

items.name: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve
items.description: State reserve of headlands, coves and trails three miles south of Carmel, with protected kelp-forest waters offshore.
items.notes: No dogs. Peak-season, holiday and weekend rates may differ.
